beats.title: Persia Builds the Royal Road
beats.description: A Persian highway with relay stations let mounted couriers carry royal messages across the empire in about a week.
beats.note: Approximate; road completed around the late 6th to early 5th century BCE

beats.title: Pheidippides Runs from Marathon
beats.description: According to legend, a Greek runner raced to Athens to announce victory over the invading Persians, then collapsed.
beats.note: Legendary; year of the Battle of Marathon

beats.title: Rome's Cursus Publicus Begins
beats.description: Rome's first emperor set up an official relay system of riders, wagons and way stations to carry state messages.

beats.title: Baghdad Starts Its Pigeon Post
beats.description: Homing pigeons were organised into a regular courier network carrying notes between distant cities of the caliphate.
beats.note: Regular Baghdad-Syria service under Nur ad-Din by 1167; earlier pigeon use in Baghdad dated to 1150

beats.title: The Mongol Yam Relay Network
beats.description: The Mongol Empire formalised a vast chain of horse stations that let riders carry orders across Asia at great speed.
beats.note: Existed under Genghis Khan; Ogedei, reigning from 1229, expanded and formalised it. No source for an exact year

beats.title: Taxis Family Opens a Post Route
beats.description: A family of Italian-born couriers set up a relay mail route between two Habsburg cities that grew into a European network.
beats.note: Route Innsbruck to Mechelen, 1490; some sources say 1489

beats.title: Beacon Fires Warn of the Armada
beats.description: A chain of hilltop bonfires carried news of the approaching Spanish fleet across England within hours.

beats.title: Royal Mail Opens to the Public
beats.description: A king allowed ordinary people to send letters through the royal postal service, for a fee paid by distance.

beats.title: London Gets a Penny Post
beats.description: A merchant launched a city mail service in which a single penny paid for a letter or parcel to be delivered within town.

beats.title: The First Mail Coach Runs
beats.description: Fast, guarded coaches replaced slow post-boys on a trial route between two English cities, speeding letters across the land.
beats.note: Trial run August 1784; regular service followed in 1785

beats.title: Chappe's Semaphore Line Opens
beats.description: Towers with movable arms relayed coded signals from hilltop to hilltop, sending news across a country in minutes.
beats.note: First message sent on the Paris-Lille line

beats.title: Cooke and Wheatstone's Telegraph
beats.description: Two Englishmen patented a telegraph using needles that pointed to letters, soon strung alongside railway lines.

beats.title: The Penny Black Stamp Appears
beats.description: Britain issued the world's first adhesive postage stamp, so senders could prepay for a letter to go anywhere in the country.

beats.title: Morse's First Telegraph Message
beats.description: From a Washington room, an inventor tapped out a famous biblical phrase over a wire to a station in another city.

beats.title: Reuters Sends News by Pigeon
beats.description: A news agency used carrier pigeons to bridge a gap in the telegraph line and beat rivals with stock prices.
beats.note: Pigeon service began 1850 between Aachen and Brussels

beats.title: Wells Fargo Opens for Business
beats.description: A California express company began carrying gold, parcels and letters by stagecoach across the American frontier.

beats.title: First Transatlantic Telegraph Cable
beats.description: A cable laid across the ocean floor let a queen and a president exchange greetings, though it failed within weeks.

beats.title: The Pony Express Launches
beats.description: Riders changing horses at relay stations raced mail across the American West between Missouri and California.

beats.title: Atlantic Cable Finally Succeeds
beats.description: After an earlier failure, a heavier cable laid by a giant steamship gave lasting telegraph contact between two continents.

beats.title: The Postcard Is Introduced
beats.description: An Austrian post office issued a card that could be sent without an envelope, cheaper and quicker than a letter.
beats.note: First official postal card, Austria-Hungary, October 1869

beats.title: Universal Postal Union Is Founded
beats.description: Countries agreed to treat international mail as one territory, with common rules and rates for letters across borders.

beats.title: Bell Patents the Telephone
beats.description: A Scottish-born inventor won the patent for a device that carried the human voice along a wire.

beats.title: Free Rural Mail Delivery Begins
beats.description: American farm families got mail delivered to their roadside boxes for the first time, instead of travelling to town.

beats.title: Marconi's Transatlantic Signal
beats.description: An Italian inventor received a faint Morse letter sent by wireless across the Atlantic Ocean.

beats.title: UPS Starts as a Messenger Service
beats.description: Two teenagers in Seattle began a bicycle messenger and delivery business that grew into a global parcel giant.

beats.title: First Official Airmail Flight
beats.description: A pilot carried sacks of letters by aeroplane at an Indian exhibition, the first officially sanctioned mail flight.

beats.title: The Zimmermann Telegram
beats.description: A coded German cable proposing an alliance with Mexico was intercepted and decoded, pushing America toward war.

beats.title: Cher Ami Delivers Her Message
beats.description: A wounded carrier pigeon flew through gunfire to save a trapped battalion and became a wartime hero.

beats.title: Transatlantic Phone Service Opens
beats.description: Callers in London and New York could speak to each other across the ocean by radio telephone for a very high price.

beats.title: China Clipper's Pacific Airmail
beats.description: A giant flying boat carried airmail from California to Asia, opening regular air service over the Pacific.
beats.note: China Clipper first transpacific airmail flight, November 1935

beats.title: First Transatlantic Telephone Cable
beats.description: An undersea cable carrying dozens of voice circuits replaced radio links between Europe and North America.

beats.title: Telstar Relays Live Television
beats.description: A communications satellite beamed live pictures and phone calls between America and Europe for the first time.
beats.note: Link/relay of signals, not broadcasting itself

beats.title: ZIP Codes Come to American Mail
beats.description: The US post office introduced five-digit codes to speed the sorting of letters by machine.

beats.title: DHL Begins Express Courier Service
beats.description: A small company in San Francisco began flying shipping documents to Hawaii, starting an international express network.

beats.title: FedEx Begins Deliveries
beats.description: A new company flew its first overnight packages from Memphis to cities across the United States.

beats.title: First Fibre-Optic Atlantic Cable
beats.description: A cable carrying pulses of light across the ocean floor greatly raised the number of calls that could cross the Atlantic.

beats.title: Western Union Ends Telegram Service
beats.description: The company that once dominated the telegraph quietly stopped sending telegrams, ending a long era of wired messages.

beats.title: India Sends Its Last Telegram
beats.description: The country's state telegraph service closed after a long run, with crowds queuing to send final messages.

beats.title: Amazon Delivers a Parcel by Drone
beats.description: An online retailer completed its first customer delivery by an unmanned aircraft, carrying a parcel to a rural home.
